name: Tuag

attributes.attribute: an Irish heroine who drew the eye of the sea god

sources: Gwynn, Edward. The Metrical Dindshenchas. Royal Irish Academy, Todd Lecture Series. Dublin: Hodges, Figgis, and Co., Ltd., 1906–1924. Reprinted Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies, School of Celtic Studies, 1991, pp. 61–63.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Tuag is an Irish heroine. At the age of 15 she drew the eye of Manannan Mac Lir, the god of the sea. She had grown up at Tara under the care of the high king Conaire. She refused every suitor. Yet Fer I, a dwarf and bard of Manannan, came to her. He sang a sleep song to her and carried her asleep away. On the way he set her down to rest. The waters of the Bann rose and took her. Her name remains on the Bann and its mouth, Tuag Inber. So she is held a river-goddess like Boand and Sinann.

okr.objective: Record the Irish heroine and river-goddess Tuag.
